question: Aman and Pawan together invested ₹76,500 in a business. At the end of the year, out of a total profit of ₹20,000, Pawan's share was ₹4,800. What was the difference between their investments?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Aman's Profit = ₹20,000 − ₹4,800 = ₹15,200.

Profit Ratio (Aman : Pawan) = 15,200 : 4,800 = 19 : 6.

Since time is equal, Investment Ratio = Profit Ratio = 19 : 6.

Total Investment = 25 parts = ₹76,500 ⇒ 1 part = ₹3,060.

Difference in investment = 13 parts = 13 × 3,060 = ₹39,780.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹39,780.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total investment = ₹76,500

Total profit = ₹20,000

Pawan's profit = ₹4,800

**Formula Used:**

Investment Ratio = Profit Ratio (when investment time periods are equal)

 Profit & Investment Proportion
 
 
 Aman (19 parts)
 Profit: ₹15,200
 
 
 Pawan (6 parts)
 Profit: ₹4,800

 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 Total Investment = ₹76,500 (25 parts)
 
 Difference = 19 − 6 = 13 parts

**Calculations:**

⇒ Aman's profit = Total profit − Pawan's profit

⇒ Aman's profit = 20,000 − 4,800 = ₹15,200

⇒ Ratio of profits (Aman : Pawan) = 15,200 : 4,800 = 152 : 48

⇒ Ratio of investments (Aman : Pawan) = 19 : 6

⇒ Let Aman's investment be 19x and Pawan's be 6x.

⇒ Total investment = 19x + 6x = 25x

⇒ 25x = 76,500 ⇒ x = 76,500 ÷ 25 = 3,060

⇒ Difference in their investments = 19x − 6x = 13x

⇒ Difference = 13 × 3,060 = ₹39,780

**∴ The correct answer is ₹39,780.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Partnership Basic Formula

Profit is distributed in the ratio of the product of Capital and Time period. Profit Ratio = (Capital₁ × Time₁) : (Capital₂ × Time₂)

Equal Time Periods

If partners invest their money for the same duration, their profits are shared directly in the ratio of their invested capitals. Capital Ratio = Profit Ratio.

Sleeping Partner

A partner who invests capital but does not manage the business is called a sleeping partner. Usually, the working partner receives a salary or fixed percentage of profit before the remaining profit is distributed as per capital ratios.
